name: get_status
title: Get status
description: Describe the game state as text: open screen, position, facing, targeted block or entity, health, inventory, whether cheats are enabled, and recent chat.

name: get_blocks
title: Get blocks
description: List the blocks in a box between two corners (inclusive), as the player's game has them loaded, grouped by block state in command syntax. Air is counted, not listed. Consecutive blocks along the x axis are merged into runs like "2..6 75 0". At most 4096 positions per call; query a single block by passing the same corner twice.

to.description: The opposite corner as [x, y, z].

name: get_surface
title: Get surface
description: Map the ground of an area from above, as the player's game has it loaded: a grid with one cell per column giving the y of its top block and a letter for what that block is (e.g. g for grass_block, with a key below). Plants, leaves, snow layers, torches, carpets and the like are skipped, so the cells show the ground under them; water and lava count as the top. Under a roof, or anywhere in the Nether, the top block is the ceiling. Use it to read terrain in one call, e.g. to find a pit or a cleared patch (exposed dirt or stone among grass), see how the ground slopes around it, or choose where to build, then use get_blocks for what's under the surface. Without from and to, maps the 25x25 columns centred on the player. At most 4096 columns per call.

from.description: One corner column as [x, z]. Give both from and to, or neither.

to.description: The opposite corner column as [x, z].

name: get_entities
title: Get entities
description: List entities (mobs, animals, dropped items, players, vehicles...) near the player, nearest first, with position, distance, health and UUID.

name: get_mob_brain
title: Get mob brain
description: Show what a mob's AI is thinking right now, as the server runs it: its attack target, the path it is walking, and then either its brain or its goals. Newer mobs (villagers, piglins, hoglins, axolotls, goats, frogs, allays, wardens, sniffers, camels, armadillos, breezes...) have a brain: active activities (e.g. core, idle, work, rest, panic, fight), running behaviors, and memories such as walk_target, attack_target, home, job_site, nearest_visible_player or hurt_by, with how long until expiring ones are forgotten. Other mobs (zombies, creepers, cows, wolves...) instead pick from goals by priority (lower first), and target goals choose whom to attack; running ones are marked. Watching a mob over several calls shows how it changes its mind. Without entity, describes the mob the player is looking at, up to 64 blocks away. Needs cheats, like run_command.

entity.description: The mob's UUID (get_entities lists them), or an entity type like "minecraft:villager" for the nearest one within 64 blocks.

name: screenshot
title: Take screenshot
description: Capture the game window as an image, along with a short status summary. By default the HUD (hotbar, chat, crosshair) is left out so the world is unobstructed; an open menu, inventory or chat screen is always shown. Cursor coordinates used by the input tool are pixels in this image.

name: run_command
title: Run command
description: Run Minecraft commands as the player and return their output: one with command, or a batch with commands, which run in order in the same game tick and carry on past any that fail. Prefer one batch to many calls when building. Needs cheats (Allow Commands) to be enabled in the world; otherwise it fails immediately, and get_status says whether commands are available. Use /help or /help <command> to discover commands and their syntax. Blocks placed with /setblock or /fill don't react to their surroundings (a lamp next to powered dust stays unlit); call update_blocks on them afterwards. Don't flip levers or buttons with /setblock either, since that skips the updates the block would send; use use_block. /fill and /setblock report failure ("No blocks were filled", "Could not set the block") when the blocks already were what they would set, which is harmless. Returns once the game shows the changes, so get_blocks, get_surface and get_entities right after see them, except that after a far /tp the chunks there take a few seconds to load and moved mobs a few ticks to get there. A batch is only an error if every command in it failed.

command.description: The command, with or without the leading slash, e.g. "/locate structure minecraft:jungle_pyramid".

commands.description: Several commands to run in order instead of command, e.g. the fills of a build.

name: use_block
title: Use block
description: Aim at a block and right-click it, as the player would: flip a lever, press a button, open a door, chest or crafting table, or use the held item on it (which places a held block against the clicked face). Aims the same way as the input action look_at_block, so the block must be in reach and not hidden behind anything; the error says why if it isn't. Returns what changed at the block and next to it (such as a placed block or the other half of a door), and a status summary.

face.description: The face to click. Defaults to the visible face pointing most toward the player.

name: input
title: Send input
description:
Perform a sequence of keyboard and mouse actions as the player, in order, then return a status summary and (by default) a screenshot. Each action except look_at_block takes at least one game tick (1/20 s); key presses, holds and waits take as many ticks as they say. A sequence can take at most 1200 ticks.

Action types:
- press {key}: press and release a key or mouse button. Combine modifiers with +, e.g. "left.control+a" or "left.shift+mouse.left".
- hold {key, ticks}: hold a key (or + combination) down for the given ticks, e.g. walking forward with w.
- key_down {key} / key_up {key}: press or release a key and leave it that way across actions, e.g. to keep sprinting.
- click {x, y, button}: move the cursor to (x, y) in screenshot pixels, then click. button is left (default), right or middle. Without x and y, clicks where the cursor is (in the world: attack/use).
- move {x, y}: move the cursor without clicking; with a mouse button held down this drags.
- scroll {amount}: scroll the mouse wheel; positive scrolls up.
- type {text}: type text into the focused text field (chat, signs, books, search boxes).
- look {yaw, pitch}: face an absolute direction in degrees; either may be left out to keep the current value.
- look_at {x, y, z}: face a point in the world.
- look_at_block {x, y, z, face}: put the crosshair on the block at these block coordinates, on a part of it that is in reach and not hidden, including thin blocks like levers, buttons and carpets. face (up, down, north, south, east or west) picks the face to aim at, which matters when placing a block against it; without it, the visible face pointing most toward you is used. Fails, and says why, if the block can't be aimed at from where you stand. It takes no tick of its own, so a click right after it, or the first tick of a hold, lands where it aimed even if the player is moving.
- wait {ticks}: do nothing for the given ticks.

Key names: letters and digits, space, enter, escape, tab, backspace, left.shift, left.control, left.alt, up, down, left, right, f1-f12, and mouse.left, mouse.right, mouse.middle.

screenshot.description: Whether to include a screenshot (without the HUD) taken after the actions.

name: update_blocks
title: Update blocks
description: Make every block in a box (at most 4096 positions) react to its surroundings as if its neighbours had just changed: redstone components re-check their power, and fences, walls, stairs and redstone dust reconnect to their neighbours. Blocks placed by /setblock and /fill usually don't do this on their own, so e.g. a lamp placed next to powered dust stays unlit until updated. It has the same side effects as real neighbour changes: observers in the box fire once, powered TNT is lit, blocks that lost their support (torches, dust, door halves) break and drop, and sand, gravel and liquids start to fall or flow. Needs cheats, like run_command. Lists the blocks in the box that changed right away.

to.description: The opposite corner as [x, y, z].
